title: Localization of a module at a multiplicative subset
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in S$, and $st\in S$ for $s,t\in S$) and $M$ an $A$-module. On $M\times S$ put $(m,s)\sim(n,t)$ iff $u(tm-sn)=0$ for some $u\in S$ (an equivalence relation). The *localization* $S^{-1}M$ of $M$ with respect to $S$ is the set of classes $m/s$ of pairs $(m,s)$, with $m/s+n/t=(tm+sn)/st$ and $(a/s)(m/t)=am/st$, an $S^{-1}A$-module and in particular an $A$-module; the *localization map* is the $A$-linear map $M\to S^{-1}M$, $m\mapsto m/1$. In particular $m/1=0$ if and only if $um=0$ for some $u\in S$, and every element of $S$ acts bijectively on $S^{-1}M$. For an $A$-linear $h:M\to N$, $S^{-1}h:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}N$ is $m/s\mapsto h(m)/s$; for $a\in A$, multiplication by $a$ on $S^{-1}M$ is $S^{-1}$ of multiplication by $a$ on $M$.
